# `pi_output_set2`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set auxiliary outputs from per-output setting objects (state, duty, PWM mode, frequency).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xf70d0, parse_gpio_value @0xe0ee0, GPIOController::WriteByIndex @0x324650, SetFreq @0x3260a0 (64-bit build) |

Object-valued variant of pi_output_set. Members are applied sequentially with no rollback. The reply is a bare success: it does not prove the hardware or frequency change was applied, because the named dslr, beep and heater branches ignore driver and frequency-setting results. As with pi_output_set, a loop-breaking error can be followed by an appended success result, producing duplicate envelope keys. The companion app sends a heater member with state, value and freq when switching the dew heater (INFERRED from the app data-transfer object).

Side effects: Writes configured output state, type, duty and PWM mode, and optionally the PWM frequency; changes can persist before a later error.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"pi_output_set2"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Object only; no positional wrapper. Each member is an object keyed by output name. Names are matched by case-sensitive substring, in order: port, dslr, beep, wide_heater, heater (heater is redirected to wide_heater when the device process type is 2). port<N> takes the first run of decimal digits as a zero-based port index. There is no gpio<N> fallback in this method. A member that is not an object fails with 107 even if its name is unrecognised; unrecognised names are otherwise ignored. An empty object succeeds. [READ] |
| `params.heater` | object | no | - | Settings for one output. Every nested key is optional; a missing or wrong-typed nested key silently keeps the initial or current value and never produces an error. For port<N> members the current values are loaded first (fallback defaults: type "other", state false, is_pwm false, value 100). dslr starts from the same defaults and forces is_pwm false after parsing. beep, heater and wide_heater start at type "other", state false, is_pwm false, value 0, then force is_pwm true and also read freq. [READ] |
| `params.heater.type` | string | no | - | Output type tag. No enumeration is enforced by the parser. [READ] |
| `params.heater.value` | number | no | - | Duty percent. No range check in the parser; with state true a computed duty outside 0..range fails with 204, with state false the duty is forced to 0. [READ] |
| `params.heater.state` | boolean\|integer | no | - | Output on/off. [READ] |
| `params.heater.is_pwm` | boolean\|integer | no | - | Select PWM (true) or digital mode. Forced by the handler for dslr (false) and for beep, heater and wide_heater (true). [READ] |
| `params.heater.freq` | integer | no | - | PWM frequency, read only for beep, heater and wide_heater members; unit not stated in the evidence (Hz INFERRED). ## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params absent, null, not an object, or a member is not an object | `expected object param` |
| 207 | Unexpected regular-expression submatch shape while extracting the port number | `fail to operate` |
| 204 | Invalid port index, or computed PWM duty outside 0..range, in the port write path | `out of limit` |
| 273 | Driver or connection failure on the checked port write branch | `GPIO operation failed` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, heater-on - Heater at 50 percent (values invented):

```json
{"id":20,"method":"pi_output_set2","params":{"heater":{"state":true,"value":50,"freq":1000}}}
```

Request, port - Digital write to port 2:

```json
{"id":21,"method":"pi_output_set2","params":{"port2":{"state":true,"is_pwm":false}}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_output_set2","result":0,"code":0,"id":20}
```

Reply, not-object:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_output_set2","error":"expected object param","code":107,"id":22}
```
